tagline: Accepted into the future, blocked by ordinary life.
paragraph: I've been following the German study since my rheumatologist first mentioned CAR-T, and honestly it's the first time in years a treatment has sounded like an actual reset rather than another drug to cycle through. I've already been on Benlysta, Saphnelo, the long course of cyclophosphamide and steroids — some worked for a while, then stopped. My kidney function isn't end-stage yet, but I'm refractory enough that my doctor said this is the most promising path to real remission. The problem is everything around the infusion. After treatment it's six to eight weeks of not being able to drive, and I'm not married, I don't have a family member who can take me back and forth, and I still have to work. Someone suggested a personal loan. Others got disqualified for the opposite reason — not sick enough, or a cancer history, a clot history, hypermobility on top of the lupus and RA. I read about a woman whose brother had CAR-T thirty years ago for cancer and still says he'd rather die than do it again, and I think about that, and then I think about another flare. I keep going back to the subreddit to read the people actually enrolled at Emory or in Belgium, asking about chemo doses and B-cell biology, because my own rheumatologists barely mention any of this. I got my hopes up high once already and it was a hard fall. I'm trying not to do that again.
patient_concerns: Six to eight weeks of no driving with no caregiver and a job to keep.
Eligibility keeps shifting: too well, too complicated, cancer or clot history disqualifies me.
Confused whether CAR-T chemo is truly heavier than the cyclophosphamide induction I already did.
Rheumatologists never sent me to a nephrologist despite stones, infections, and borderline kidney function.
person_concerns: Afraid to hope again after the last trial rejection knocked me flat.
Watching trial enrollees online while feeling like a spectator to my own cure.
Tired of cycling through Benlysta, Saphnelo, steroids and waiting for each to fail.
Dreaming of being actually healed, not just stabilized between flares.
